attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given in his own voice. They are not a quote of WIRED or of anyone else.

semantics.note: An unhedged statement about the scope of the jailbreak problem: it is shared across generative AI and not specific to Anthropic. The normalised version keeps that scope without adding to it.

contract.note: The plain reading is that LLMs from several developers share the vulnerability. That is the ordinary meaning in context, which talks about LLMs. The May 2026 snapshot was chosen by the evaluator but is reasonable. The stronger reading, that no generative system could ever be safe, is not tested, and the contract flags this.

evidence.note: Cisco's cross-vendor evaluation was published May 27, 2026. It tested 15 flagship models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Amazon and xAI, and every model showed non-trivial multi-turn attack success. That covers at least four developers other than Anthropic. Exact experiment dates are not given, but the work describes the frontier as of the target month.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs evidence of successful guardrail bypasses in models from at least two developers other than Anthropic, in the target period. Cisco's independent evaluation from May 2026 found successful multi-turn attacks on every model it tested, from OpenAI, Google, Amazon and xAI as well as Anthropic. The packet contains no counterevidence. The claim is supported under the plain reading. The stronger reading, that perfect safeguards are impossible in principle, is not assessed.
